_note: Organic gap materials that branch nodes consume and no other production file makes. Yields are physical (cited in each yield_basis); labour is borrowed from a named neighbouring entry, or left out and said so.

silkworm_eggs_kg.basis: per 100 kg of fresh cocoons set aside as seed and allowed to hatch, mate and lay, output as kg of eggs
silkworm_eggs_kg.yield_basis: SEED REARING, the grainage: cocoons kept for breeding are not stifled, the moths emerge, pair and lay on cloth or paper and the eggs are stored cool until spring. A fresh cocoon weighs about two grams, so 100 kg is about fifty thousand cocoons, half of them female; a female lays several hundred eggs of about half a milligram each, which is on the order of 5 kg of eggs in all (an estimate from those three figures, not checked against a source). The cocoons are not sold as silk, so they enter as a material input at the cocoon entry's own price. LABOUR: the sorting, pairing, laying and egg storage by hand, taken as about 150 artisan-hours (an estimate; none could be sourced). Made only where sericulture is held, so a society without the worm prices it as if it were. Conf C.

ramie_stock_kg.basis: per hectare of ramie nursery per year, output as kg of rhizome cuttings for planting out
ramie_stock_kg.yield_basis: GROWN. Ramie is a perennial that spreads by rhizome and is propagated by dividing it, not by seed; an established stand yields a standing crop of rhizome many times what it takes to plant the same area again. 2000 kg of cuttings per hectare-year is an order-of-magnitude estimate, not checked against a source. LAND: the batch is one hectare-year, converted to hectare_land's unit as in wheat_kg's LAND note. LABOUR: lifting, dividing and bundling the rhizome by hand, taken as about 400 labourer-hours (an estimate). Made only where ramie is already grown, so the stock cannot be had without a society that holds it. Conf C.

draught_animal_kg.basis: per hectare of breeding pasture per year, output as kg of live weight of working cattle and horses reared to work age
draught_animal_kg.yield_basis: GROWN on pasture by a breeding herd: cows and mares calve or foal, the young are reared on grass and hay to work age. Live-weight gain on extensive pasture is on the order of 100 kg per hectare per year (an estimate, not checked against a source). LAND: the batch is one hectare-year, converted to hectare_land's unit as in wheat_kg's LAND note. LABOUR: herding, calving and breaking to harness, taken as about 40 labourer-hours (an estimate). The animals' own feed is the pasture, charged as land. Made only where draught power is held, because a society with no animal to breed cannot start a herd by labour. Conf C.

cashmere_goat_kg.basis: per hectare of breeding pasture per year, output as kg of live weight of fine-undercoat goats reared to breeding age
cashmere_goat_kg.yield_basis: GROWN on pasture by a breeding flock: does kid and the young are reared on browse and grass to breeding age. The yield and the labour are borrowed from the draught_animal_kg entry (about 100 kg of live weight per hectare of extensive pasture a year, an estimate, not checked against a source); a goat is smaller than a head of cattle but is stocked more densely, so the per-hectare weight is taken as the same. LAND: the batch is one hectare-year, converted to hectare_land's unit as in wheat_kg's LAND note. LABOUR: herding, kidding and shearing or combing, taken as about 40 labourer-hours (an estimate). Made only where the fibre is already produced, because a society with no breeding goats cannot start a flock by labour. Conf C.

angora_goat_kg.basis: per hectare of breeding pasture per year, output as kg of live weight of Angora goats reared to breeding age
angora_goat_kg.yield_basis: GROWN on pasture by a breeding flock: does kid and the young are reared on browse and grass to breeding age. The yield and the labour are borrowed from the draught_animal_kg entry (about 100 kg of live weight per hectare of extensive pasture a year, an estimate, not checked against a source); a goat is smaller than a head of cattle but is stocked more densely, so the per-hectare weight is taken as the same. LAND: the batch is one hectare-year, converted to hectare_land's unit as in wheat_kg's LAND note. LABOUR: herding, kidding and shearing or combing, taken as about 40 labourer-hours (an estimate). Made only where the fibre is already produced, because a society with no breeding goats cannot start a flock by labour. Conf C.

jute_seed_kg.basis: per hectare of jute grown for seed per year, output as kg of seed
jute_seed_kg.yield_basis: GROWN. A jute crop left to flower and ripen for seed, not cut for fibre, yields a few hundred kilograms of seed per hectare; 400 kg is an order-of-magnitude estimate, not checked against a source. LAND: the batch is one hectare-year, converted to hectare_land's unit as in wheat_kg's LAND note. LABOUR: borrowed from wheat_kg's 150 labourer-hours per hectare of hand-tilled field crop; seed threshing and cleaning is not added, so labour is understated. Made only where jute is already grown. Conf C.

hop_rhizome_kg.basis: per hectare of hop nursery per year, output as kg of rhizome cuttings for planting out
hop_rhizome_kg.yield_basis: GROWN. A hop stand is propagated from cuttings of its rootstock; a nursery hectare yields cuttings for planting several hectares of garden. 500 kg of cuttings per hectare-year is an order-of-magnitude estimate, not checked against a source. LAND: the batch is one hectare-year, converted to hectare_land's unit as in wheat_kg's LAND note. LABOUR: twice wheat_kg's 150 labourer-hours per hectare, for the digging, cutting and bundling of rootstock by hand (an estimate). Made only where hops are already grown. Conf C.

pyrethrum_stock_kg.basis: per hectare of pyrethrum nursery per year, output as kg of crowns and seed for planting out
pyrethrum_stock_kg.yield_basis: GROWN. Pyrethrum is propagated by dividing established crowns or by seed; a nursery hectare yields stock for planting several hectares. 300 kg per hectare-year is an order-of-magnitude estimate, not checked against a source. LAND: the batch is one hectare-year, converted to hectare_land's unit as in wheat_kg's LAND note. LABOUR: twice wheat_kg's 150 labourer-hours per hectare, for lifting, dividing and bundling by hand (an estimate). Made only where pyrethrum is already grown. Conf C.

mulberry_leaves_kg.basis: per hectare of intensively pruned mulberry orchard per year, output as kg of fresh leaf
mulberry_leaves_kg.yield_basis: GROWN. The 20-30 tonnes of leaf per hectare per year for an intensively pruned orchard is the figure silk_kg's own yield_basis uses; the low end is taken. LAND: the batch is one hectare-year, converted to hectare_land's unit as in wheat_kg's LAND note. LABOUR: 150 labourer-hours per hectare for the orchard's tillage, pruning and manuring (borrowed from wheat_kg's field labour) plus about 800 for picking: the leaf is stripped by hand, and 20,000 kg at about 25 kg per worker-hour is 800 hours (an order-of-magnitude estimate; not checked against a source, none could be opened). Conf C.

pyrethrum_flower.basis: per hectare of pyrethrum (Chrysanthemum cinerariifolium) per year, output as kg of dried flower heads
pyrethrum_flower.yield_basis: GROWN. Established pyrethrum stands are usually quoted at roughly 500-1500 kg of dried flower per hectare per year; the lower-middle of that range is taken for unimproved stock. Pyrethrins are a fraction of a percent to about 1-2 percent of the dried flower, which downstream extraction consumes. LAND: the batch is one hectare-year, converted to hectare_land's unit as in wheat_kg's LAND note. LABOUR: borrowed from wheat_kg's 150 labourer-hours per hectare of hand-tilled field crop; harvest and processing work specific to this crop is not added, so labour is understated. Conf C.

hops.basis: per hectare of hop bine per year, output as kg of dried cones
hops.yield_basis: GROWN. Traditional hop gardens yielded on the order of 1000-1500 kg of dried cones per hectare per year (about 10-12 hundredweight per acre in older English records); the middle is taken. LAND: the batch is one hectare-year, converted to hectare_land's unit as in wheat_kg's LAND note. LABOUR: borrowed from wheat_kg's 150 labourer-hours per hectare of hand-tilled field crop; harvest and processing work specific to this crop is not added, so labour is understated. Conf C.

mat_sugar.basis: per hectare of sugar cane per year, output as kg of raw (muscovado-type) sugar boiled from pressed juice
mat_sugar.yield_basis: GROWN, then pressed and boiled in the field-side works. Hand-and-animal-mill cane of the pre-industrial period runs on the order of 30-40 tonnes of cane per hectare, of which roller crushing and open-kettle boiling recover roughly 5-6 percent as crystallised raw sugar, giving about 2 tonnes per hectare. Boiling heat is supplied by burning the crushed cane (bagasse), which the crop itself provides, so no thermal input is charged. LAND: the batch is one hectare-year, converted to hectare_land's unit as in wheat_kg's LAND note. LABOUR: borrowed from wheat_kg's 150 labourer-hours per hectare of hand-tilled field crop; harvest and processing work specific to this crop is not added, so labour is understated. Conf C.

mat_opium.basis: per hectare of opium poppy per year, output as kg of dried raw opium latex
mat_opium.yield_basis: GROWN. Hand-lanced poppy capsules give on the order of 10-25 kg of raw opium per hectare in traditional cultivation; 15 kg is taken. LAND: the batch is one hectare-year, converted to hectare_land's unit as in wheat_kg's LAND note. LABOUR: borrowed from wheat_kg's 150 labourer-hours per hectare of hand-tilled field crop; harvest and processing work specific to this crop is not added, so labour is understated. Conf C.

tobacco_extract.basis: per hectare of tobacco per year, output as kg of nicotine recovered in the extract
tobacco_extract.yield_basis: GROWN, then leached. Pre-industrial tobacco yielded roughly 1000 kg of cured leaf per hectare; cured leaf holds about 2 percent nicotine by mass, and leaching or steam distillation recovers about 80 percent, so 1000 x 0.02 x 0.8 = 16 kg of nicotine. Waste stems and dust carry the same alkaloid at lower grade, which this basis does not distinguish. LAND: the batch is one hectare-year, converted to hectare_land's unit as in wheat_kg's LAND note. LABOUR: borrowed from wheat_kg's 150 labourer-hours per hectare of hand-tilled field crop; harvest and processing work specific to this crop is not added, so labour is understated. Conf C.

foxglove_leaf_kg.basis: per hectare of cultivated foxglove (Digitalis purpurea) per year, output as kg of dried leaf
foxglove_leaf_kg.yield_basis: GROWN. Cultivated foxglove, a biennial harvested for its leaf, is commonly cited at about 1-2 tonnes of dried leaf per hectare per year; the midpoint is taken. Glycoside content is a fraction of a percent of the dried leaf and is left to the consuming node. LAND: the batch is one hectare-year, converted to hectare_land's unit as in wheat_kg's LAND note. LABOUR: borrowed from wheat_kg's 150 labourer-hours per hectare of hand-tilled field crop; harvest and processing work specific to this crop is not added, so labour is understated. Conf C.

potato_starch_kg.basis: per hectare of potatoes per year, output as kg of washed, dried potato starch
potato_starch_kg.yield_basis: GROWN, then rasped and washed. Pre-industrial potato yields are on the order of 10 tonnes of tubers per hectare; tubers are about 17 percent starch by mass and rasping and washing recovers about 85 percent, so 10000 x 0.17 x 0.85 = 1445 kg. LAND: the batch is one hectare-year, converted to hectare_land's unit as in wheat_kg's LAND note. LABOUR: borrowed from wheat_kg's 150 labourer-hours per hectare of hand-tilled field crop; harvest and processing work specific to this crop is not added, so labour is understated. Conf C.

starch_kg.basis: per tonne of dry wheat starch by wet extraction (dough washed under water, starch settled and dried)
starch_kg.yield_basis: COMPOSITION. Wheat grain is about 68 percent starch by mass and washing dough out recovers about 88 percent of it, so about 0.60 kg of starch per kg of grain, i.e. 1000 / 0.60 = 1667 kg of wheat per tonne. The gluten and bran left over have a use of their own, which is not credited here, so the grain charge is if anything high. Washing, settling and drying labour has no cited figure and is left out, so labour is understated. Conf C.

arsenopyrite_kg.basis: per tonne of hand-dressed arsenopyrite (FeAsS) ore, about 60 percent FeAsS by mass
arsenopyrite_kg.yield_basis: EXTRACTED. Arsenopyrite is a heavy, metallic, easily hand-sorted sulphide of the same vein class as stibnite. The 60 percent dressed grade and the miner and labourer hours are borrowed from stibnite_kg's entry, the nearest hand-dressed sulphide ore. Conf C.

arsenic.basis: per tonne of white arsenic (arsenic trioxide, As2O3) sublimed from roasted arsenopyrite
arsenic.yield_basis: STOICHIOMETRY. FeAsS is 74.92/162.83 = 46.0 percent arsenic and As2O3 is 75.7 percent arsenic, so a tonne of As2O3 holds 757 kg of arsenic, which is 1646 kg of pure FeAsS or 2743 kg of 60 percent ore; roasting in air drives the oxide off as vapour, condensed in flues, and about 80 percent is recovered, so 2743 / 0.8 = 3429 kg of ore. Roasting sulphide ore is largely self-heating, so no thermal input is charged. Furnaceman hours are borrowed from antimony_kg's roast-and-reduce entry. Conf C.

mat_potash.basis: per tonne of crude potash (mostly potassium carbonate) leached from wood ash and boiled dry
mat_potash.yield_basis: COMPOSITION AND LATENT HEAT. Hardwood ash carries on the order of 10 percent potassium carbonate by mass, and leaching recovers about 85 percent, so 1000 / (0.10 x 0.85) = 11765 kg of ash per tonne. Leach liquor of about 12 percent salt has 1/0.12 - 1 = 7.33 kg of water to boil off per kg of potash at 2.257 MJ/kg latent heat, giving 16540 MJ, a physical floor before any pot efficiency. The ash itself is 1 percent of the wood burned (see wood_ash_kg), which is why potash was a byproduct of land clearing rather than a fuel-fed industry. Leaching and stirring labour has no cited figure and is left out, so labour is understated. Conf C.

basic_slag_kg.basis: per tonne of phosphatic converter slag, with the steel blown alongside it (basic-lined converter on high-phosphorus pig iron)
basic_slag_kg.yield_basis: MASS BALANCE. Blowing high-phosphorus pig iron (about 2 percent P) in a lime-lined converter leaves roughly 200-250 kg of slag per tonne of steel, so a tonne of slag comes with about 4.5 tonnes of steel; the pig iron charge is 4.5 t over an about 90 percent metal yield = 5000 kg. About 100 kg of phosphorus becomes about 230 kg of P2O5, i.e. 23 percent of the slag, and the lime flux (about 500 kg) supplies the rest of the slag's calcium oxide. Blowing is exothermic (silicon, carbon and phosphorus burn), so no thermal input is charged. Furnaceman hours are steel_plate_kg's 25 per tonne of steel, scaled to 4.5 t. Conf C.

wood_tar_kg.basis: per tonne of pine wood tar from a tar kiln, with the charcoal left in the kiln
wood_tar_kg.yield_basis: PYROLYSIS. Resinous pine burned slowly in a closed kiln drains about 10 percent of its mass as tar, and the residue is charcoal at the same 25 percent of wood mass charcoal_kg's clamp burn uses, so 10000 kg of wood gives 1000 kg of tar and 2500 kg of charcoal. Labour is charcoal_kg's 30 collier-hours per 4000 kg of wood, scaled to 10000 kg. Conf C.

bentonite_kg.basis: per tonne of swelling (montmorillonite) clay dug from a pit
bentonite_kg.yield_basis: EXTRACTED. Dug like any pit clay; the labour is borrowed from clay_kg's entry. Conf C.

mat_bentonite_slurry.basis: per tonne of drilling-mud slurry at 5 percent bentonite by mass
mat_bentonite_slurry.yield_basis: COMPOSITION. Slurry for supporting an open trench is made at a few percent bentonite by mass in fresh water; 5 percent is taken, so 50 kg of clay in 950 kg of water. Mixing labour and energy are not cited and are left out. Conf C.

mat_gutta_percha.extracted_from: forest (Palaquium latex, coagulated in hot water)
mat_gutta_percha.basis: per tonne of raw gutta-percha coagulated from Palaquium latex
mat_gutta_percha.yield_basis: EXTRACTED from wild trees by bleeding or felling; a tree gives only kilograms, so a tonne stands for hundreds of trees. The 60 hours are borrowed from resin_kg's tapping entry (the nearest latex-bleeding work) and badly understate a felling-and-collecting trade at that yield. Conf C.

mat_iodine_compound.basis: per tonne of iodine, as iodide salt, recovered from kelp ash
mat_iodine_compound.yield_basis: EXTRACTED. Burnt kelp ('kelp' in the Scottish sense) carries on the order of 0.5-1 percent iodine by mass, and leaching plus crystallisation recovers most of it; at 0.75 percent about 133 tonnes of kelp ash stand behind a tonne, itself burnt from a couple of dozen times its mass of wet weed. LABELLED HEURISTIC for the labour (no cited figure): gathering and burning about 3200 tonnes of wet weed per tonne of iodine at roughly a tonne of wet weed gathered, spread to dry and burnt per labourer-day of ten hours, plus leaching and crystallising the ash, comes to about thirty thousand labourer-hours. Conf C.

horn_kg.basis: per kg of the cleaned raw material
horn_kg.yield_basis: Horn sheaths are slaughter offcuts: cattle horn cores are loosened by soaking and the keratin sheath pulled off. The animal's or person's keep is charged elsewhere. Labour is borrowed from bone_kg's 0.3 hours per kg of separating a raw slaughter byproduct; it understates the cleaning work for gut and shell. Conf C.

mat_animal_gut.basis: per kg of the cleaned raw material
mat_animal_gut.yield_basis: Sheep or ox intestine is stripped and cleaned as a slaughter byproduct. The animal's or person's keep is charged elsewhere. Labour is borrowed from bone_kg's 0.3 hours per kg of separating a raw slaughter byproduct; it understates the cleaning work for gut and shell. Conf C.

shell_kg.basis: per kg of the cleaned raw material
shell_kg.yield_basis: Mother-of-pearl and other shell is gathered from shore or shallows and sorted by hand. The animal's or person's keep is charged elsewhere. Labour is borrowed from bone_kg's 0.3 hours per kg of separating a raw slaughter byproduct; it understates the cleaning work for gut and shell. Conf C.

human_hair_g.basis: per 1000 g of the cleaned raw material
human_hair_g.yield_basis: Human hair for instrument use is cut, degreased and sorted. The animal's or person's keep is charged elsewhere. Labour is borrowed from horsehair_kg's 1.0 hours per kg (cut, sort, clean hair); it understates the cleaning work for gut and shell. Conf C.

cacao_kg.basis: per hectare of cacao orchard per year, output as kg of fermented, sun-dried beans
cacao_kg.yield_basis: GROWN. Theobroma cacao is an understorey tree of the wet lowland tropics, frost-tender and needing year-round warmth and rain, which the Koppen classes Af, Am and Aw describe (Soconusco, the Gulf coast and Tabasco, from which Mexica tribute drew cacao, are Am and Aw), so a territory holding none of them cannot grow it. Traditional shaded orchards under tall trees, without fertiliser, give on the order of 200 to 500 kg of dry beans per hectare a year; 300 is taken. Labour is pruning and weeding, picking and splitting the pods, heap fermentation of the pulp-covered beans for about five days and sun-drying them; about 125 worker-days (1000 hours) per hectare-year is an order of magnitude, as for the pepper garden. The dry bean is about a gram, so a kilogram is about a thousand beans (the bean-counting money of Mesoamerica). LAND: the batch is the one hectare-year of the basis, charged at hectare_land's own rent, which is arable land's rent and so a labelled heuristic for a tropical orchard. SOURCES: agronomic figures from memory of the cacao agronomy literature (Wood and Lass, Cocoa, 4th ed., 1985) and the Florentine Codex book 8 and 10 on cacao use and counting; NONE OF THESE COULD BE OPENED for this entry (Complaints/347). Conf C.
